title: Decompose 19 oversize Python source files to clear the file-size allowlist (refresh of #3111)
summary: v1 task breakdown for #3312. Decomposes ALL 19 allowlisted oversize Python files (issue table, live counts verified in the refine analysis 2026-06-26) into sub-packages following the canonical pattern (docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md + the merged template PR #2335 + worked reference scripts/select_tests/), driving scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml's files: map to EMPTY. SCOPE IS LOCKED by operator directive + the resolved refine HITL: no descope, no deferral of the structural outliers (pipelines.py ~27.2k, gateway.py ~10.4k), and _run_pipeline is addressed head-on (non-negotiable #7). Structured as 19 independent per-file decomposition slices (one phase == one slice == one PR), ordered easiest->hardest (smallest line count first; the two outliers last) so independent slices land value even if pipelines.py/gateway.py stall again — exactly the ordering heuristic the issue recommends given the failed-attempt history (#2817 implement-phase failure, #3111 never run). The pattern-adoption parent that anchored the #2261 DAG is ALREADY MERGED (#2335), so there is NO parent slice and NO inter-slice DAG dependency: slices are siblings, mutually independent at the source level, conflicting ONLY mechanically on scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml (resolved by the section-(e) rebase recipe). Each slice: external-importer audit -> step-0 git mv baseline commit -> cluster extraction with explicit per-symbol re-export barrel -> allowlist-entry drop + CLAUDE.md seam coverage -> make lint + make test-all green. Acceptance carried from the refine analysis (AC-1..AC-7). The architect owns the technical slice DAG / cluster shapes; this artifact owns the per-file task decomposition, ordering, and PR packaging (one PR per file).

scope_notes.in_scope: All 19 files in the issue table (live counts in the refine analysis are authoritative; the issue table is a snapshot). Each decomposed into a sub-package with an __init__.py re-export barrel + underscore-prefixed private submodules per docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md. Allowlist files: map driven to empty. Concrete CLAUDE.md seam coverage for every in-scope file: rows in orchestrator/CLAUDE.md + gateway/CLAUDE.md, a NEW seam table in sandbox/CLAUDE.md, and a NEW shared/CLAUDE.md. _run_pipeline phase-transition state machine split directly inside the pipelines.py slice (non-negotiable #7). gateway.py @app.route decorators stay in __init__.py with bodies delegating to submodules (non-negotiable #8). make lint + make test-all green at every landing boundary. Pure refactor.
scope_notes.out_of_scope: Behavior changes (pure refactor; bugs surfaced get a separate 'Part of #3312' follow-up issue, never bundled). Test file size (lint exempts test_*.py / *_test.py / tests/**). Non-Python files (JSON/YAML/Markdown). Decomposing files NOT in the 19-file table. Retargeting #2562 / retagging docs/ #2261 refs is optional bookkeeping, NOT an acceptance gate (see grounding correction).
scope_notes.binding_decisions: Operator directive (contract task_description) + resolved refine HITL decision-1 (2026-06-26): scope = all 19 files including pipelines.py (~27k) and gateway.py (~10k); _run_pipeline tackled head-on; NO descoping; planner owns ordering/packaging only, not scope reduction. Pattern HITL decisions carried from #2261 via the pattern doc: decision-1 (sub-package not sibling files), decision-5 (explicit per-symbol re-exports), decision-6 (underscore-prefixed submodules), decision-7 (barrel is the stable public API), decision-8 (route decorators stay in __init__.py).
scope_notes.grounding_correction_honored: The refine analysis corrected a stale issue claim: orchestrator/CLAUDE.md and gateway/CLAUDE.md do NOT currently carry '#2261 slice-N / TBD' placeholder rows (those #2261 refs live in docs/, not the seam tables). So the seam-table work is CREATE concrete submodule rows per landing, not RETAG existing placeholder rows. sandbox/CLAUDE.md exists with no seam table (add one); shared/CLAUDE.md is ABSENT (create it). Binding criterion: concrete seam coverage exists for every in-scope file at its landing.
scope_notes.ordering_rationale: Front-load independent per-file slices, structural outliers last (issue 'History' recommendation + refine 'planner owns' note). Given two prior attempts never landed a single decomposition slice, ordering easiest->hardest maximizes banked value: 17 simpler files can land even if pipelines.py/gateway.py stall a third time. The outliers are NOT dropped — they are scheduled last, still in scope, with their own enriched task sets.

grounding.pattern_doc: docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md (present, 13,292 bytes) — canonical recipe: (a) sub-package layout, (b) step-0 git mv to __init__.py as its own bisectable baseline commit, (c) method-modules-on-class pattern for class-dominated files, (d) external-importer git grep audit, (e) allowlist-drop + parallel-slice rebase recipe, (f) routes-handling convention (decorators in __init__.py), (g) further-split in-slice rather than a fresh allowlist entry, (h) follow-up-issue convention for surfaced bugs.
grounding.worked_reference: scripts/select_tests/ — __init__.py barrel + __main__.py + _cli.py/_constants.py/_graph.py/_io.py private submodules; already absent from the allowlist. Copy this exact shape. tests/tools/select_tests/ is the canonical scenario-organized test example (no retrofit required).
grounding.template_pr: PR #2335 (merged 2026-04-30) — pattern-adoption parent. Coder MUST read its diff before the first decomposition slice.
grounding.live_sizes_authoritative: Refine analysis table (verified 2026-06-26, this worktree): 19 files, 9 over the byte cap (pipelines.py, gateway.py, orch_cli.py, gateway_client.py, signals.py, kubernetes_spawner.py, mcp_tools.py, worktree_manager.py, peer_consensus.py). Caps: hard_lines 1500 / hard_bytes 100000. Counts drift UP between snapshots (lint ratchets non-allowlisted files but lets allowlisted ones grow); the coder re-checks live size at slice start.
grounding.back_compat_surface: Refine re-derivation: routes.pipelines.* ~57 distinct patch targets across ~137 test files (dominant surface); gateway.gateway.* ~12 distinct patch targets. These are sizing estimates; the coder re-runs the section-(d) audit per cluster at implement time (counts shift as main drifts). Every extracted symbol with an external reference is re-exported through the barrel so unittest.mock.patch keeps resolving.
grounding.run_pipeline: pipelines.py contains the _run_pipeline phase-transition state machine — the hardest piece, mechanical extraction won't work, deferral OFF the table (non-negotiable #7). Prior design (pattern doc) splits it into per-phase handlers + a thin orchestration loop (the _run_loop.py / per-cluster shape). Addressed directly inside the pipelines.py slice (phase-19).
grounding.claude_md_targets: orchestrator/CLAUDE.md (12 files), gateway/CLAUDE.md (3 files), sandbox/CLAUDE.md (3 files; add seam table), shared/CLAUDE.md (1 file; create new).

approach.slice_model: 19 per-file decomposition slices (one phase == one slice == one PR), ordered easiest->hardest. SERIALIZED into a single linear dependency chain slice-1 -> slice-2 -> ... -> slice-19: every slice edits scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml (each removes its own entry), so per #3046 the slices must be ordered along one chain — independent branches off the shared base would collide at integration on that file. No pattern-adoption parent (merged in #2335). The chain preserves easiest-first ordering so 17 simpler files bank value before the two structural outliers, which sit at the tail.
approach.per_slice_template: Every slice follows the same five-task internal shape parameterized on the file F: (1) external-importer audit (git grep every public symbol in F), (2) step-0 git mv F.py -> F/__init__.py as a standalone green baseline commit, (3) cluster extraction into _<cluster>.py submodules + explicit per-symbol re-export barrel, (4) allowlist-entry drop + CLAUDE.md seam-table row (further-split in-slice if any submodule lands over the cap; never a fresh allowlist entry), (5) make lint + make test-all green; mechanical test patch-path rewrites in-slice, test-logic rewrites filed as follow-ups.
approach.pr_packaging: One PR per slice (per file). Each PR drops exactly one allowlist entry and adds exactly one file's seam coverage. The terminal-state acceptance check (allowlist files: map empty) is satisfied cumulatively as the 19th PR lands. Branches prefixed egg/. PR titles: 'refactor(<area>): decompose <file> into a sub-package (Part of #3312)'.
approach.outlier_handling: gateway.py (phase-18) and pipelines.py (phase-19) carry enriched task sets: pre-allocated cluster lists, the route-decorator convention (gateway), and the _run_pipeline per-phase-handler split (pipelines). They remain single slices each but with explicit further-split tasks because mechanical extraction alone will leave submodules over the cap.

non_goals: No descope: every one of the 19 files, including pipelines.py (~27.2k) and gateway.py (~10.4k), is in scope; none are deferred to a follow-up (operator directive + resolved refine HITL).
No behavior changes (pure refactor); surfaced bugs are separate follow-ups.
No decomposition of test files (lint-exempt) or non-Python files.
No decomposition of files outside the 19-file table.
No new layout invented — the canonical sub-package + re-export-barrel pattern (PR #2335 / docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md) is followed exactly.
risks_for_reviewers: Re-export drift is the dominant risk: a missed re-export surfaces as AttributeError in a test that patches the moved symbol. Mitigation: the per-slice external-importer audit (task-N-1) + explicit per-symbol re-exports (decision-5) + make test-all gate. pipelines.py (~57 targets) is the highest-exposure slice — scheduled last, after the pattern is proven on 17 simpler files.

_run_pipeline behavior risk: splitting a phase-transition state machine with subtle ordering. Mitigation: per-phase handlers stay private and are exercised through the existing dense seam coverage; pure-refactor discipline; scheduled last (phase-19).

Allowlist YAML is the only cross-slice contention point. With parallel slices it conflicts mechanically every time. Mitigation: section-(e) rebase recipe (take 'theirs' for other slices' removals, re-apply own). NOT a logical dependency — slices stay independent.

Submodule-over-cap after extraction: a naive split leaves a submodule still over the cap. Mitigation: per-slice task to verify EVERY submodule under BOTH caps + further-split in-slice (section-(g)), never a fresh allowlist entry; outliers (phases 18-19) have explicit further-split tasks.

Sub-package circular imports may surface latent cycles masked by the single-file shape (esp. pipelines.py / gateway.py). Mitigation: the existing routes/phases.py lazy/dual-import precedent; one consistent import style per sub-package.

Failed-attempt history (#2817 implement-phase failure, #3111 never run, #2902 closed unmerged after main drift): main can drift under a long-running slice. Mitigation: easiest-first ordering banks value early; each slice rebases + re-runs the live audit at start; outliers land last so their longer review windows don't block the 17 simpler wins.

entrypoint.py / orch_cli.py have script-execution entry points (container ENTRYPOINT / console scripts) that a package conversion can break — flagged in those slices' step-0 tasks; mirror scripts/select_tests/'s __main__.py.

ordering.rationale: Easiest -> hardest by line count; the two structural outliers (gateway.py, pipelines.py) last. Front-loads independent per-file wins so 17 files can land even if the outliers stall a third time, exactly as the issue 'History' section recommends.
ordering.dependency_model: Single linear chain: phase-N depends on phase-(N-1). Forced by #3046 because all 19 slices edit scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml. Ordering is easiest->hardest by line count; the two outliers (gateway.py, pipelines.py) are the chain tail, fully in scope, so a stall there does not block earlier landings.
ordering.pr_packaging: One PR per slice (per file). Each PR: drops exactly one allowlist entry + adds exactly one file's seam coverage + is independently make-lint/make-test-all green. The empty-allowlist acceptance criterion is satisfied cumulatively when phase-19's PR lands.
